outcome: Redington tunes a small open model on curated examples entirely on the institution’s own hardware, so domain knowledge never leaves the boundary.
overview: Some institutions cannot send their text to a hosted model — the data is licensed, personal or simply not permitted to leave — and a general-purpose assistant trained on the open internet does not know their domain anyway. Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI packages a small open model with a tuning workflow that adds domain knowledge from curated examples, running entirely on the institution’s own hardware. The result is a model that stays inside the boundary and speaks the institution’s vocabulary. Redington sizes the accelerator requirement and takes one narrow domain through tuning and evaluation before anything wider is proposed.

benefits.text: Domain text never leaves the institution, because tuning and inference both run on its own hardware
benefits.limits: True of the deployment; it says nothing about the licensing of the source data itself, which remains the institution’s question

benefits.text: A small tuned model can outperform a larger general one on a narrow domain task
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Entirely dependent on the quality and coverage of the curated examples; without an evaluation set this claim cannot be tested at all

benefits.text: Accelerator requirements stay modest because the model is small by design
benefits.limits: Modest relative to frontier-model training, not relative to a server refresh; the sizing exercise is what makes this concrete

residency: Tuning corpus, model weights and inference all remain on institution-controlled hardware; nothing is sent to a hosted inference service

notFor.situation: An institution permitted to use a hosted model service for the data in question
notFor.why: On-premises tuning carries hardware and operating cost that a hosted service does not; residency is the reason to accept it

notFor.situation: A use case that needs broad general knowledge rather than domain depth
notFor.why: A small tuned model trades breadth for depth; asking it for breadth is asking for the thing it gave up

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Red Hat implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a tuned model scored against an independent evaluation set
Support model: Vendor subscription support for the platform; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional tuning-cadence retainer with the domain team.
1) Assessment — domain selection, example availability, evaluation-set design and accelerator sizing
2) Design — tuning workflow, versioning, evaluation protocol and serving path
3) Build — platform install, base model, tuning pipeline and local endpoint
4) Tune and hand over — two cycles scored against the evaluation set, workflow handed to the domain team
deliverables: Every tuned version is traceable to the base model and the example set that produced it
Each version is scored against the independently authored evaluation set, including the untuned base
Inference runs entirely within the institution’s network boundary, evidenced by network configuration
